q: The fundamental structural and functional unit of life is the:
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
Robert Hooke coined 'cell' in 1665 after observing dead cork cells.
Organisms made up of a single cell are called:
A single-celled organism is called unicellular.
Mycoplasma (about 0.3 μm) is the smallest known cell.
Cell theory was originally proposed by:
Schleiden and Schwann together proposed cell theory.
Who was the first person to see and describe a live cell?
Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell.
The longest cell in the human body is the:
The nerve cell (neuron) is the longest human cell.
Which of these is considered the largest isolated single cell known?
The (unfertilised) egg of an ostrich is the largest known single cell.
The outermost layer of the prokaryotic cell envelope is the:
The glycocalyx is the outermost layer of the cell envelope.
The size (S value) of a prokaryotic ribosome is:
Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits.
The parts of a bacterial flagellum are:
A bacterial flagellum has a filament, hook and basal body.
Reserve material in a prokaryotic cell is stored as:
Inclusion bodies, freely suspended in cytoplasm, store reserve material in prokaryotes.
Mesosomes are formed by the extension of the:
Mesosomes are infoldings/extensions of the plasma membrane.
Bacteria which do not take up the Gram stain are called:
Bacteria that fail to take up Gram stain are Gram negative.
The middle layer of the prokaryotic cell envelope, which determines cell shape, is the:
The cell wall, the middle layer, gives the cell its shape and structural support.
A slime layer, when it becomes especially thick and tough, is more specifically called a:
The glycocalyx exists as a loose slime layer in some bacteria, or as a thick, tough capsule in others.
The plasma membrane is mainly composed of a:
The plasma membrane is fundamentally a lipid bilayer, with proteins and carbohydrates.
The fluid mosaic model of the membrane was proposed by:
Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972.
The cell wall is present in:
The cell wall occurs in plant and fungal cells, exterior to the plasma membrane.
The middle lamella mainly consists of:
The middle lamella, cementing neighbouring plant cells, is mainly calcium pectate.
Channels connecting the cytoplasm of neighbouring plant cells are called:
Plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells through the cell wall.
Integral proteins lie buried within the lipid bilayer, unlike peripheral proteins which sit on the surface.
Facilitated diffusion of polar molecules across a membrane is carried out by:
Carrier proteins facilitate diffusion of polar molecules that cannot cross the lipid bilayer directly.
The disc-shaped sacs making up the Golgi apparatus are called:
Cisternae are the stacked, disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi apparatus.
Lysosomes are packed with hydrolytic (digestive) enzymes.
The membrane of the vacuole is called the:
The tonoplast is the vacuole's surrounding membrane.
SER is the major site for:
Smooth ER is the chief site of lipid synthesis.
The 'forming face' of the Golgi apparatus is the:
The cis (convex) face is the forming face, receiving material.
Lysosomes are formed as a result of packaging by the:
Lysosomes are vesicles formed by packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
In Amoeba, excretion is carried out mainly by the:
The contractile vacuole in Amoeba is used for excretion (and osmoregulation).
Glycoproteins and glycolipids are synthesised in the:
The Golgi apparatus synthesises glycolipids and glycoproteins, besides packaging materials.
The ER divides the intracellular space into which two compartments?
The ER divides the intracellular space into luminal (inside the ER) and extra-luminal (cytoplasmic) compartments.
George Palade first observed ribosomes under an electron microscope.
Ribosomes are made of RNA and proteins.
The Svedberg unit (S) indicates a particle's:
The Svedberg unit reflects a particle's density and size (sedimentation behaviour).
Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cell for their role in ATP production.
The infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane are called:
Cristae are the infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S, made of 60S and 40S subunits.
Mitochondria divide by fission, independent of the cell cycle.
Mitochondria are the principal site of aerobic respiration, producing ATP.
The prokaryotic 70S ribosome comprises 50S and 30S subunits.
Plastids occur in plant cells and euglenoids.
The green-coloured plastid, containing chlorophyll, is the:
The colourless plastid used mainly for storage is the:
Chloroplasts in a leaf are found chiefly in the:
Mesophyll cells of the leaf are the main site of chloroplasts.
A stack of thylakoids is called a:
A granum is a stack of thylakoids, like a pile of coins.
Structures connecting thylakoids of different grana are called:
Stroma lamellae are tubules connecting thylakoids across different grana.
The chloroplast's inner membrane, as compared to the outer membrane, is:
The inner chloroplast membrane is less permeable than the outer membrane.
The number of chloroplasts per cell in Chlamydomonas is typically:
Chlamydomonas typically has just 1 chloroplast per cell.
The space enclosed within a thylakoid membrane is called the:
The thylakoid's internal space is called the lumen.
The DNA found in the chloroplast's stroma is:
Chloroplast stroma has its own small, circular DNA, distinct from nuclear DNA.
The '9+2' array refers to the arrangement of microtubules in the:
The axoneme (core of cilia/flagella) shows the 9+2 microtubule arrangement.
The centrosome contains two structures called:
The structure from which cilia and flagella emerge is called the:
The basal body, a centriole-like structure, is where cilia/flagella originate.
A centriole is made up of how many peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein?
A centriole has 9 peripheral fibrils, each a triplet, in a cartwheel arrangement.
Each peripheral fibril of a centriole is a:
Each of the 9 peripheral fibrils of a centriole is a triplet of microtubules.
During cell division, centrioles help form the:
Centrioles help form the spindle fibre during cell division.
The nucleus is bound by the:
The nuclear envelope, made of two membranes, bounds the nucleus.
The site of active rRNA synthesis within the nucleus is the:
The nucleolus is the site of rRNA synthesis.
The primary constriction of a chromosome is called the:
The centromere is the primary constriction of a chromosome.
Chromatin is present during which phase of the cell cycle?
Chromatin, the loose nucleoprotein network, is present during interphase.
A chromosome with the centromere at the very terminal end is called:
Telocentric chromosomes have a terminal centromere.
On the sides of the centromere
Disc-shaped kinetochores are present on the sides of the centromere.
A chromosome is composed of DNA, histone proteins, non-histone proteins, and:
Chromosomes contain DNA, histone and non-histone proteins, and some RNA.
The human genome is distributed among how many pairs of chromosomes?
Humans have 23 pairs (46 total) of chromosomes.
The scientist who discovered the nucleus was Robert ______.
According to Virchow's modification, all cells arise from ______ cells.
Virchow established that cells only arise from pre-existing cells, ruling out spontaneous generation.
The main structural support and shape of a bacterial cell is provided by the:
The cell wall (middle layer of the envelope) gives the prokaryotic cell its shape and support.
A prokaryotic ribosome is made of a 50S and a ______ subunit, together forming a 70S ribosome.
50S + 30S subunits together form the 70S prokaryotic ribosome.
Bacteria that do not take up the Gram stain are called Gram ______ bacteria.
Bacteria failing to take up the Gram stain are Gram negative.
The two types of endoplasmic reticulum are:
ER is classified as Rough ER (ribosome-studded) and Smooth ER (no ribosomes).
The contractile vacuole of Amoeba primarily functions in:
The contractile vacuole expels excess water and wastes, aiding excretion/osmoregulation.
The Golgi's ______ face is the maturing face, from which vesicles are released.
The trans face is the maturing/releasing face of the Golgi apparatus.
The double membrane system is a structural feature of the:
Mitochondria have a characteristic double-membrane structure.
Which feature is shared by BOTH mitochondrial ribosomes and prokaryotic ribosomes?
Mitochondrial ribosomes, like prokaryotic ribosomes, are 70S — a key piece of evidence for the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria.
Which of these is NOT found in the mitochondrial matrix?
Chlorophyll is a chloroplast pigment, not present in mitochondria.
Ribosomes were first observed by ______, under an electron microscope.
A potato tuber's plastids, storing starch, are an example of:
Starch-storing leucoplasts in tubers are called amyloplasts.
The main pigment associated with chloroplasts is:
Chlorophyll is the defining pigment of chloroplasts, giving them their green colour.
The flat, membrane-bound tubules connecting thylakoids of different grana are called ______.
Stroma lamellae connect thylakoids belonging to separate grana.
The chloroplast's stroma contains its own small, circular DNA and ______ ribosomes.
Chloroplast ribosomes, like those of mitochondria and prokaryotes, are 70S.
Cilia and flagella are covered externally by the:
Both cilia and flagella are covered by the plasma membrane, continuous with the rest of the cell surface.
The main function of cilia, described as working 'like oars', is:
Cilia's oar-like beating produces motility (movement of the cell, or of fluid past the cell).
Each peripheral fibril of a centriole is a bundle of three microtubules, called a ______.
Each of a centriole's 9 peripheral fibrils is a triplet of microtubules.
Sieve tube cells of vascular plants are notable for lacking a:
Mature sieve tube cells lack a nucleus, similar to mammalian RBCs.
The disc-shaped structures on the sides of the centromere are called ______.
Kinetochores are disc-shaped structures flanking the centromere.
The term 'cell' was first coined by:
Robert Hooke coined the term 'cell' in 1665.
The scientist who discovered the nucleus is:
The largest known single cell is:
The ostrich egg is the largest known single cell.
PPLO and Mycoplasma are examples of:
PPLO and Mycoplasma are prokaryotic organisms.
The subunits of a 70S prokaryotic ribosome are:
A 70S ribosome is made of 50S and 30S subunits.
A bacterial flagellum has three parts: the filament, the hook and the:
The three parts of a bacterial flagellum are the filament, hook and basal body.
The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by:
Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model.
Water moves across the plasma membrane mainly by:
Water crosses membranes chiefly via osmosis.
The plant cell wall's primary component is:
Cellulose is the main component of the plant cell wall.
The endomembrane system does NOT include the:
The mitochondrion is excluded from the endomembrane system.
RER, with its ribosomes, is the site of protein synthesis.
The vacuolar membrane is called the:
The tonoplast is the vacuole's surrounding membrane.
The eukaryotic ribosome's Svedberg value is:
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are green.
The chloroplast's own DNA and ribosomes are located in the:
The stroma contains the chloroplast's small circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
The number of peripheral microtubule pairs in an axoneme is:
The axoneme has 9 peripheral pairs plus 1 central pair (9+2 array).
Centrioles form the basal body of cilia/flagella and also help form the:
Centrioles help form the spindle fibre during cell division.
Mammalian RBCs and sieve tube cells are notable because they lack a:
Both mammalian RBCs and sieve tube cells lack a nucleus.
The nuclear matrix, consisting of the nucleolus and chromatin, is called the:
The nucleoplasm is the nuclear matrix, made of the nucleolus and chromatin.
A chromosome's primary constriction is called the:
The centromere is the chromosome's primary constriction.
The fluid mosaic model was proposed by:
They have their own DNA and 70S ribosomes.
The arrangement of microtubules in a cilium is:
A chromosome with one extremely short arm is:
Acrocentric: centromere close to one end.
Enzymes that work at acidic pH are found in:
Lysosomal hydrolases are active at acidic pH.
Infoldings of the bacterial plasma membrane.
A cell with 70S ribosomes and no nucleus is:
A cell lacking centrioles and having a large vacuole:
Chromosome with centromere at the tip is:
Organelle with its own DNA, making ATP:
Cell organelle rich in hydrolytic enzymes:
Glycosylation of proteins mainly occurs in:
RBCs swell in plain water due to:
An organelle with grana and stroma:
The cell theory was proposed by Schleiden and ____.
'Omnis cellula e cellula' was said by:
The fluid mosaic model was proposed by:
Name the site of ribosomal RNA synthesis.

The nucleus was first described by:
